title: The family photo table
summary: Help set up a family photo table for a small community exhibition. Read the approved card list and a signed note. Use the bags and cups in the photos to match people with cards. Ask for help with two cards, then change your plan when one photo is private. All photo details are in the texts.

documents.title: Approved card list
documents.text: Family photo table. Set up on Saturday at 10:00. The exhibition opens at 11:00. This list gives the words for three cards. Write one name and one short line on each card. The first card is for Tom. Write Tom on the top line and With his red bag below it. The second card is for Lina. Write Lina and With her blue bag. The third card is for Ben and Jo. Write Ben and Jo and With their yellow cups. The card for Ben and Jo is a spare. Keep it in the green box until you need it. The cards for Tom and Lina are ready on the table.

documents.title: Lina’s signed note
documents.text: Hello, table helper. Please take my photo off the table before the exhibition opens. It is the photo with my blue bag. My sister gave me this photo. I want to keep it at home. Please put the photo and my name card in the white envelope. Leave the envelope in the drawer under the table. You can put the photo of Ben and Jo on the table in its place. Their card is in the green box. Tom’s photo can stay on the table. I can pick up my envelope from 12:00 to 12:15 on Saturday. Thank you for your help. Signed, Lina.

recordings.title: A visitor points out two photos
recordings.text: Excuse me. I know the two people in these photos. Both photos show a garden and a long bench. Look at the photo on the left. Tom is next to the bench. His red bag is on the bench. Now look at the photo on the right. That’s Lina. She is at the back of the garden, by the wall. Her blue bag is on the ground by her feet. There’s a tree in each photo, so the tree doesn’t help much. The bags are easy to see. A friend is coming at 11:10. I’d like to show him where to find the family table.

recordings.title: A volunteer’s voice message
recordings.text: Hello, this is Eva, the table volunteer. I can bring two stands to the family table at 10:15. One stand is tall and one is short. They are both white. Please put the tall stand at the back of the table and the short one at the front. Put one photo on each stand. The name cards can lie flat in front of the stands. There is a space by the door for the green box. Please leave it there after you take out any card you need. I leave the room at 10:30. You can tell me your plan when I bring the stands.

reading.prompt: First read Approved card list to see what it is for. What does the list help you do?
options: Find the room for the exhibition
Write the cards for the photos
Choose clothes for a family photo
Pick up a photo after the exhibition
reading.explanation: The list gives a name and a short line for each card.

reading.prompt: Read Approved card list again. Make three columns for the names, the things and the card locations. Which short line goes under Lina?
reading.explanation: The second card has Lina’s name above the line With her blue bag.

reading.prompt: In Approved card list, where can you get the card for Ben and Jo if you need it?
options: On the table beside Tom’s card
In a bag under the bench
At the door with the visitor
reading.explanation: The list tells you to keep their spare card in the green box.

reading.prompt: Read Lina’s signed note. What is Lina’s main request?
options: Put her photo next to Tom’s photo
Write a new card for her sister
Take her photo off the table before opening
Move her photo to the back of the table
reading.explanation: Lina asks the table helper to take her photo off the table before opening.

reading.prompt: Read Lina’s signed note again. Make brief notes under Photo, Card and Envelope. Where does the envelope go?
options: On the table with the spare card
In the drawer under the table
In the green box near the table
reading.explanation: The note says to leave the white envelope in the drawer under the table.

reading.prompt: In Lina’s signed note, when can Lina collect her envelope? Add the pickup time to your notes.
reading.explanation: Lina gives a Saturday pickup window from 12:00 to 12:15.

reading.prompt: Put these three events in order in your notes. Use Approved card list and Lina’s signed note. Which order is correct?
reading.explanation: Setup is at 10:00, opening is at 11:00, and pickup starts at 12:00.

listening.prompt: Listen to A visitor points out two photos once. What does the visitor help you do?
options: Know which garden photo shows each person
Plan a visit to the garden
Choose where to put the stands
Pack the photo table at the end
listening.explanation: The visitor points out Tom in one garden photo and Lina in the other.

listening.prompt: Listen to A visitor points out two photos again. Write one clue under Left and one under Right. What is on the bench in the left photo?
listening.explanation: The visitor says Tom is in the left photo and his red bag is on the bench.

listening.prompt: In A visitor points out two photos, which clue helps you find Lina in her photo?
options: She is by the bench at the front.
She is by the wall at the back.
She is next to Tom’s red bag.
She is on the left with yellow cups.
listening.explanation: The visitor says Lina is at the back of the garden by the wall.

listening.prompt: Listen to A volunteer’s voice message once. What should you be ready to tell Eva when she brings the stands?
options: How to get to the garden
listening.explanation: Eva says you can tell her your plan when she brings the stands.

listening.prompt: Listen to A volunteer’s voice message again. Draw two spaces called Back and Front. Where does the short stand go?
options: At the back of the table
At the front of the table
listening.explanation: Eva asks for the short stand at the front of the table.

listening.prompt: In A volunteer’s voice message, where do the name cards go? Add two small marks to your drawing.
options: Flat in front of the stands
Behind the photos on the stands
On the floor by the door
listening.explanation: Eva says the name cards can lie flat in front of the stands.

listening.prompt: Listen to A volunteer’s voice message one more time. Write Bring and Leave by the two times you hear. When does Eva leave the room?
listening.explanation: Eva brings the stands at 10:15 and says she leaves at 10:30.

grammar.focus: His, her and their before a thing word
grammar.explanation: Use his, her or their before a word for a thing. These small words tell us who the thing belongs to. Use his for Tom, a man. Say his bag. Use her for Lina, a woman. Say her bag. Use their when the thing belongs to Ben and Jo together. Say their card for one card or their cups for two cups. Look at the people first. One person can have two bags. Two people can have one card. Read the three photo cards again. Mark his, her and their. Then say the name or names for each word.

examples.before: Tom has a red bag. Her bag is on the bench.
examples.after: Tom has a red bag. His bag is on the bench.
examples.why: The bag belongs to Tom, so use his before bag.

examples.before: Lina has an envelope. His envelope is in the drawer.
examples.after: Lina has an envelope. Her envelope is in the drawer.
examples.why: The envelope is for Lina, so use her before envelope.

examples.before: Ben and Jo share a card. Her card is in the box.
examples.after: Ben and Jo share a card. Their card is in the box.
examples.why: Both people share one card, so use their before card.

questions.prompt: Eva has two pens for the cards. Which line tells us where Eva’s pens are?
options: His pens are by the box.
Their pens are by the box.
Her pens are by the box.
She pens are by the box.
questions.explanation: Both pens belong to Eva, so use her before the plural word pens.

questions.prompt: Ben has a coat. Eva hangs the coat by the door. What can Eva write about Ben?
options: His coat is by the door.
Her coat is by the door.
He coat is by the door.
Their coat is by the door.
questions.explanation: The coat belongs to Ben, so use his even though Eva hangs it up.

questions.prompt: Lina and Tom have one box for their family cards. Which words can you put under both names on the box?
questions.explanation: Lina and Tom share the box, so use their for the one box.

questions.prompt: Tom brings a bag for Lina. The bag belongs to Lina. Finish the line about the bag. Tom puts ___ bag on a chair.
questions.explanation: Lina owns the bag, so use her even though Tom puts it down.

questions.prompt: Ben and Jo have four photos in one folder. What can Eva say about the photos?
options: He photos are in the folder.
Her photos are in the folder.
Their photos are in the folder.
His photos are in the folder.
questions.explanation: The photos belong to Ben and Jo together, so use their before photos.

questions.prompt: Tom has a green pen and a black pen. Which question asks about both of Tom’s pens?
questions.explanation: Tom owns both pens, so his comes before pens in the question.

questions.prompt: The note belongs to Eva. Choose the sentence that shows it is Eva’s note.
questions.explanation: Eva writes and signs the note herself, so her note refers to Eva.

questions.prompt: Tom and Ben share a table. Eva has a chair. Fill the two spaces in order. This is ___ table. That is ___ chair.
questions.explanation: Tom and Ben share the table, and the chair belongs to Eva.

grammar.transfer: Make a short lost property list for Eva. Tom has a black hat. Lina has a red scarf. Ben and Jo share one blue umbrella. Write each name or set of names, then write a line about the thing with his, her or their. Cover the names, read the lines, then uncover the names and check each word.

vocabulary.example: I keep a photo of my dad by my bed.

vocabulary.example: My name card is beside my plate.

vocabulary.example: I put my phone on a stand.

vocabulary.meaning: on the side of your right hand

The wet pages lie flat on the kitchen table.

speaking.audience: Eva, the volunteer who brings the stands
speaking.first: Both photos show a garden bench. On the left, Tom’s red bag is on the bench. On the right, Lina is by the wall with her blue bag at her feet. Write one clue for the left photo and one for the right photo. Say to Eva, “Can you match these two cards?” Pause. Read Eva’s practice question aloud, “Which card goes on the left?” Answer in one or two short sentences. Then read and answer, “What about the right?”
speaking.change: At 10:20, you find Lina’s signed note. A helper puts the photo of Ben and Jo beside the green box in a clear sleeve. Their name card is in the box.
speaking.second: Take a second turn as yourself. First ask Eva for the card from the green box. Then answer her practice question, “Which two photos go on the stands now?” Keep Tom in your plan. Say which stand you want for each photo and where Lina’s envelope goes.
checklist: Use the red bag and blue bag to match the first two cards.
Pause after the request and answer each practice question in a short turn.
Say his bag or her bag in the first take and their card in the second take.
Name Tom and Ben and Jo as the two photos for the stands.
Say where Eva can find the spare card and where Lina’s envelope goes.

writing.audience: The volunteer who checks the table before the exhibition opens
writing.first: Read Approved card list. Eva has a tall stand for the back and a short stand for the front. Each card lies flat in front of its photo. Copy the exact words for Tom’s and Lina’s cards. Put each name on its own line above its short line. Make a small two-line plan with Back and Front. Put Tom at the back and Lina at the front. Add a line with the opening time.
writing.change: At 10:20, you read Lina’s note. The helper puts the photo of Ben and Jo beside the green box. The white envelope is ready in the drawer under the table.
writing.second: Write a clean set of labels and a new table plan in about 25 to 45 words across several lines. Keep Tom at the back and keep the opening time. Change the front photo and card. Add a short reminder about the drawer and Lina’s pickup window.
checklist: Give each public card a name line and the exact short line from the list.
Put Tom on the tall back stand and Ben and Jo on the short front stand.
Put Lina’s photo and card in the white envelope in the drawer.
Give Lina’s pickup window as 12:00 to 12:15.

immersion.role: Family photo table helper just before opening
immersion.goal: Set up the table for the first visitors. Make a plan that a new helper can follow, with the right cards and a short private note for Lina’s pickup.
constraints: The exhibition opens at 11:00 on Saturday.
The public photos are Tom and Ben and Jo. Use their approved card words.
Use the card clues to match Tom with his red bag and Ben and Jo with their yellow cups.
Lina’s photo and card go in the white envelope in the drawer. Keep her pickup details on the helper’s note.
There is space for one flat photo on the left of the table. Leave room beside it for its card.
immersion.change: At 10:55, the tall stand breaks. You still have the short stand at the front. Tom’s photo can lie flat on the left. Ben and Jo’s photo must stand up because their clear sleeve is wet underneath. In the photo, Ben and Jo each hold a yellow cup.
deliverables: Make one small plan with three spaces marked Back, Front and Left. Show where the two photos and their cards go. Mark the back space empty.
Write two public cards with two lines each. Then cover the approved list and match each card to a photo using its bag or cups clue.
Write one private helper note with the envelope color, its two contents, the place to find it and Lina’s full pickup window.
Read your plan aloud in two short turns. First tell the helper where the photos go. Then tell the helper where to put the two public cards.
checklist: Show Ben and Jo on the only working stand at the front.
Show Tom flat on the left with his card beside his photo.
Put the card for Ben and Jo flat in front of the short stand.
Check that his goes with Tom and their goes with Ben and Jo.
Keep Lina’s photo and name card out of the public plan and in the white envelope.
Check that the helper’s note gives 12:00 to 12:15 for pickup.
